status: frozen before the first recorded baseline trial; any change is recorded under amendments with a reason
questions: Q1 Where does one CloudProof Raft group saturate?
Q2 What dominates latency before and after saturation?
Q3 Can group commit, replication pipelining and bounded batching raise throughput without breaking durability or linearizability?
Q4 What gap remains versus etcd under comparable conditions on the same machine?
Q5 Does every optimization survive the deterministic correctness and fault-testing suite?

systemUnderTest.topology: 3 voting replicas, one Raft group, native `node replica/index.js` processes on one machine, loopback TCP, fresh data directory per trial
systemUnderTest.clientPath: HTTP/1.1 keep-alive to the leader; the generator is told the leader once the no-op has committed
systemUnderTest.durabilityContract: A write is acknowledged only after it is committed: stored durably (fsync) on a majority of voters, including every copy that is counted. Unchanged by every optimization; group commit changes when fsync happens, never whether an acknowledged entry was fsynced.
systemUnderTest.instrumentation: RAFT_PERF=1 for every trial (observational; see replica/raft-perf.js)
systemUnderTest.logging: replica stdout/stderr redirected to a per-replica file, as a container would

workload.operation: PUT /kv/:key with body {"value": <payload>} -> Raft entry {op: set}; no clientId/seqNo
workload.rationaleForNoClientId: matches etcd Put semantics (last-writer-wins, no server-side deduplication) so the etcd comparison is like for like. The exactly-once path (clientId+seqNo) is measured separately and reported as its own result.
workload.payloadDefinition: length of the ASCII value string; the replicated entry and the HTTP body are larger (key, op, JSON framing)
workload.keyChoice: round robin over k0..k999 by global arrival index

loadGeneration.model: open loop, constant inter-arrival time 1/rate, arrivals interleaved across generator processes
loadGeneration.latencyDefinition: end-to-end latency = response completion - intended arrival time (coordinated-omission free); service latency = completion - socket write, reported separately
loadGeneration.timeouts: an arrival without a response 10 s after its intended time is abandoned and recorded in the all-requests distribution at exactly 10 s
loadGeneration.histogram: log-linear, exact below 2048 us, <= 0.1% relative error above (replica/perf-histogram.js); percentiles report the bucket upper bound
loadGeneration.generatorHealth: every trial records generator lag (dispatch - intended); p99 lag > 5 ms marks the trial generator-saturated

trial.warmupExcluded: generators count only arrivals intended inside the window; every replica's /perf window is reset at the window start
trial.pointAggregation: latency percentiles from the merged histograms of all repetitions (pooled); throughput/CPU as mean with min/max across repetitions; no trial is ever selected or discarded

stabilityRule.text: A trial is stable iff (a) OK completions inside the window reach >= 98% of the offered rate, (b) errors + timeouts <= 0.5% of measured arrivals, (c) end-to-end p99 over all measured arrivals (timeouts at the timeout bound) < 1000 ms, and (d) the median OK latency of the last fifth of the window is <= 2x that of the first fifth, unless that last-fifth median is <= 20 ms. A point is stable when a majority of its repetitions are.

stopRule.text: A curve stops after two consecutive majority-unstable rates, or after any rate whose mean achieved/offered ratio is below 0.5. Every rate that is run uses the full repetition count.

kneeDefinition: the highest ladder rate that is majority-stable and whose every lower ladder rate is majority-stable; max stable throughput = mean achieved throughput at that rate

saturationFractions.text: after a curve's ladder is complete, 0.5x and 0.8x its knee (rounded) are run with the same repetitions; 'p99 at 50%/80% of saturation' is read from those points, never interpolated

configurations.ablation: cumulative: baseline -> +group commit -> +pipelined replication -> +bounded batches with coalesced replication trigger -> +framed TCP transport (= all optimizations)
configurations.extra: baseline + framed TCP transport only, to isolate the transport's contribution when disk is the bottleneck
configurations.payloadCoverage: baseline and all-optimizations: 64 B, 1 KiB, 16 KiB. Intermediate ablation steps and transport-only: 1 KiB only (time budget; 1 KiB is the canonical comparison payload).

profiles.method: V8 CPU profile of the leader through the inspector, exactly covering a 15 s measurement window, 250 us sampling
profiles.points: A = 0.5 x knee (sub-saturation), B = knee (near saturation), C = the first unstable ladder rate (overloaded), 1 KiB payload, for the baseline and the all-optimizations configuration
profiles.storage: processed summaries committed; raw .cpuprofile and folded stacks kept locally, identified by SHA-256

comparisonMetrics: p99 at 0.5x knee, 0.8x knee and at the knee
leader CPU percent of one core and CPU microseconds per op
cluster fsyncs per second and fsyncs (log + metadata) per committed op
AppendEntries RPCs per second and per committed op, entries per RPC
replication bytes per committed op (TCP payload bytes on follower sockets)

etcd.condition: run only after this methodology is frozen and the CloudProof sweeps are complete
etcd.plan: 3-member etcd cluster on the same machine and drive, same open-loop generator speaking etcd's v3 HTTP/JSON gateway (POST /v3/kv/put), same payloads, rates, windows, repetitions and stability rule
mismatchesToDisclose: transport (grpc-gateway translation vs direct HTTP handler)
persistence (WAL + bbolt vs line log + JSON metadata)
hardware sharing (all members on one machine)
